newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end up on Japan news, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end up on Japan news, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: Reaction to news Japan will exempt some pork imports from tariffs during August kept CME lean hog futures strong into the close while late position rolling made for a mixed close in pork bellies, traders said.
Hog futures closed 0.700 to 0.050 cent per lb higher with August up 0.650 at 82.025 cents. Pork bellies finished off 0.625 to up 0.725 with only August off at 83.950 cents.

Japan's agriculture minister said the exemption on pork import tariffs was needed to lower domestic pork prices, which rose sharply after Japan banned imports of pork from Taiwan and lower pork production was forecast this summer.

Although some traders said August is too short a period to move large amounts of pork, others speculated Japan would keep tariffs off as long as needed to pull down prices there. This kept hog futures strong.

"Their summer production is down and that's not something that's going to change overnight so why should they just leave it (tariff exemption) on for 30 days and not just extend it for September or October or however long it's going to take to cool off their own wholesale market," said Chuck Levitt, livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
However, late fund selling and light profit-taking pared best levels with Rand Financials on both sides of the market, pit sources said.
In hog options, commission house sold October 70 puts and 72 calls, December 74 calls and February 72 calls. Iowa Grain sold October 74 calls, pit sources added.

Pork bellies also showed were buoyed by the Japan news but the advance was also tied to reduced hog slaughter rates attributed to tight market-ready hog supplies. However, August tumbled late as one house rolled long August positions into February and hit sell stops in August, traders said.

The rolling in August was attributed to reduction of positions ahead of its spot position on Friday. This offset support that developed when IBP Inc announced Monday it was reducing hog slaughter hours further at its plants. Other meat companies had also cut hours due to the low hog numbers.
"When you cut back the slaughter you are going to produce less fresh product right in the middle of the bacon, lettuce and tomato season," Levitt said.

After the close, the CME reported last week's out-of-town storage movement at a net out-movement of 3.467 million lbs, above the high end of estimates of 2.8 million to 3.2 million. The figure compares with a 3.402-million-lb out movement during the comparable week last year.
RBH actively spread short August/long February late, pit sources said.
